findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _overridden (the FAIL check and the R6-2 reach see only the FAILs of the trace being checked); README 'A gate's FAIL is never overridden' ('every step holding the failed artefact's own bytes, at any time and of any kind'; 'The FAIL reaches into a delegated loop that runs after it') and 'Not claimed'
findings.finding:
A delegated loop's FAIL does not reach its parent. C705: the parent's patch (X) passes schema-check and is handed to a delegation. The child holds X, its unit-tests FAILs X, and it revises and delivers Y. The parent then writes patch (X) and delivers patch. Accepted. C705c, the same steps in one loop, is refused GATE_OVERRIDDEN.
The child runs under the parent's profile, its trace is part of the parent's record (checked by digest), and a gate on the same bytes decides the same. So the parent overrides a deterministic FAIL recorded in its own run. Round 7 made the parent's FAIL reach a later child (R6-2), not the reverse. The README's own-bytes reach is not limited to one trace, and 'Not claimed' does not state the limit.

findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _overridden, the R6-2 reach (only the taint enters the child; the child's own re-gate sees only the child's FAILs); README 'The FAIL reaches into a delegated loop that runs after it' and 'Every gate that failed the bytes of a revision's chain, on any step holding them, must pass the revision's bytes before they are used'
findings.finding:
The re-gate stops at the delegation boundary. C701: unit-tests FAILs patch (X) in the parent. A later delegation runs a child that regenerates X, and the child's schema-check FAILs it. The child revises it (Y), which passes schema-check only, writes Y and reports. The parent builds on the report and delivers. Accepted. C701c, the same steps in one loop, is refused GATE_OVERRIDDEN: unit-tests failed the bytes of the revision's chain and never passes Y.
The R6-2 reach exempts the child's revision, as in one loop. But that revision is then re-gated only against the child's own FAILs. So a revision that read bytes the parent's gate failed reaches a write without that gate, which R6-1 (2) closed in one loop. C701b (the child's revision also passes unit-tests) is accepted.
findings.requiredChange:
When the parent's FAIL reaches a child that holds the failed bytes, require the parent's failing gates to pass a child revision whose chain holds those bytes before its use in the child. Pin C701. Or state the limit under 'Not claimed'.
Checked: the same sketch (the child's re-gate takes the parent's earlier failing gates by bytes, `_regate(cv, extra)`) refuses C701 and accepts C701b and round-6 T604b.

findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _overridden, the re-gate (`if r["revises"] is None or r["produces"] is None: continue`); README 'A revision that did not succeed has no artefact and is not used'
findings.finding:
Round 7 skips every revision without an artefact, not only one that did not succeed. A MODEL step may succeed with no artefact (a plan step does). R711: unit-tests FAILs patch; r1 revises it (OK, produces null), reading patch and the diagnosis as a revision may; write-file consumes r1; a final model step built on the write is gated and delivered. Accepted. The round-6 model refuses it (GATE_OVERRIDDEN).
Controls:
- R711c, the same revision recording its artefact Y (schema-check passes it), is refused;
- R711b, a fresh step without an artefact reading the failed patch, is refused.
So recording no artefact lets the answer to a FAIL reach a write that the gate that failed never checked. Round 6 already accepted R711d, where unit-tests 'passes' the artefact-less r1 (a gate on a step without an artefact is accepted, round-6 S611).
findings.requiredChange:
Require a successful revision to carry its artefact (refuse it otherwise, for example as REVISION_BOUND: a revision answers a FAIL with new bytes). Then only a revision that did not succeed is skipped, as the README says. Pin R711 as a refusal vector.
Checked: one line in the sketch's _revision_bound refuses R711 and R711d as REVISION_BOUND. The vectors, the builder's isolation and all earlier probes are unchanged.

findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _overridden, the R6-2 reach (`for s in later:` with `_View(v.child(s), ...)` inside the loop over failing gates)
findings.finding:
The reach into children runs once per FAIL and per later delegation, and each pass rebuilds the child's view from the profile's tool and hook lists. So it is quadratic in steps and linear in profile size. Measured: g FAILs on one subject, then g delegations whose children hold the failed bytes.
- Profile of 4 tools: g = 125 takes 0.046 s, 250 takes 0.166 s, 500 takes 0.644 s, 1,000 takes 2.47 s, and 2,000 (4,003 steps) takes 10.0 s.
- Profile padded to 4,004 tools: g = 125 takes 0.89 s, 250 takes 10.3 s, and 500 takes 32.1 s. Without FAILs, the existing per-child checks take 4.4 s for 250 delegations and 17.9 s for 1,000 (linear).
Extrapolated, not run: about 7 minutes at 2,000 FAILs and 2,000 delegations under a 4,004-tool profile.
findings.requiredChange: Build each child's view once per delegation, and check each distinct failed digest once (group the parent's earlier FAILs by bytes). The sketch does this: 500/500 at 4,004 tools takes 8.8 s (the existing per-child cost), and 2,000/2,000 takes 3.2 s. Optionally check the stored profile once per trace check rather than once per child.

findings.location: README 'A gate's FAIL is never overridden' and 'Not claimed'
findings.requiredChange: Name these under 'Not claimed' (a delegated loop is covered only by the reaches the README states), or close them, for example by applying the byte rules over the parent's steps with each child's steps placed at its delegation.

findings.location: README 'A gate's FAIL is never overridden', the paragraph after the bullets; scripts/agent_loop.py _tainted docstring
findings.finding:
Two wording points.
(1) The README breaks 'so a tool output / that merely repeats / derived bytes' over a two-word source line. It renders as one paragraph, but it is a stray rewrap.
(2) R6-3 added 'later' to the README only. The `_tainted` docstring still says 'every model or delegation step whose artefact repeats the bytes of another tainted step' (its 'in one pass in append order' implies the direction).
findings.requiredChange: Rewrap the paragraph, and say 'every later model or delegation step' in the docstring.

dispositions.evidence: The re-gate hunk equals the round-6 sketch alt2's byte for byte, apart from comments and the docstring (diff of WORK/alt2 against the round-7 model). R601, R602, R604 and R605 are refused GATE_OVERRIDDEN, and R606 is accepted. R603 is refused too (the optional delivery of a holder). V139 (R601) and V140 (R605) pin the class, and the README states the rule. A 20,000-trace random differential against round 6 differs only in the intended classes. New: the skip also covers successful revisions without an artefact (R7-3).

alt2's delegation hunk is adopted verbatim. T604 is refused, and V141 pins it with stored child child-run-14. T604b is accepted. Two new checks agree: C706 (a read-only relay inside the child) is refused, and C707 (a child that only reads the bytes) is accepted. The README states the reach as specified. Remaining boundary cases: R7-1, R7-2 and R7-5.
The README now says 'every later model or delegation step' and that derived bytes are 'matched forward only'. T601 is accepted and T601b refused, as before. The docstring nit is R7-6.

The re-gate takes the first passing run per gate ID and one reach pass per revision. Measured: g = u = 680 takes 0.49 s (round 6: 14.6 s), and g = u = 1,365 (4,096 steps) takes 2.06 s. The round-6 series at 200 takes 0.047 s (round 6: 0.431 s). 819 revised chains take 2.52 s and 1,365 distinct artefacts 0.86 s. The new R6-2 reach has its own super-linear path: R7-4.

_unsafe_retry refuses a launched NATIVE write that ended UNKNOWN when its retry changes the input. O601 is now refused UNKNOWN_SIDE_EFFECT_RETRIED, and V142 pins it under the new fixture profile native-write-loop (put-object, WRITE, NATIVE). O701 (the same input) and O702 (a FAILed native write retried with another input) are accepted. O704 (a second retry that changes the input) is refused. The README and the docstring state the rule.
The round-5 probes (A-E, 40) re-run on round 7 are identical to round 6. The round-5 timing cases are unchanged: 2,048 failing gates in 4,096 steps take 2.37 s, and 300 producers take 0.011 s.
The round-4 probes (35) re-run on round 7 are identical to round 6. The round-4 fixpoint timings are at most 0.128 s.
The round-3 probes Q01-Q33 re-run on round 7 are identical to round 6, apart from Q31's case count (148 refusal traces).

The round-1/2 probes P01-P40 and N01-N31 re-run on round 7 are identical to round 6, apart from N31, which lists the new stored child child-run-14 (ok), and P34's timings. The 193 round-6 vectors are kept byte for byte (55 renumbered by +4 after the four inserted at V139-V142).
